You will help design technical training and communications throughout the organization, striving to cultivate a company-wide security culture where all employees share responsibility for safeguarding and protecting us. Based in New York City, this hybrid role involves regular in-person office visits to host group training sessions and individual meetings with staff. Who are we? Enterprise Technology enables the people, platforms, and practices that support The New York Times' journalism and business operations. We partner with departments across the company to help employees work securely,, and productively through thoughtful technology solutions. We support the systems and capabilities that keep us running while looking for new ways to reduce friction and improve the daily experience of our workforce. The Education team's mission is to help our technical and non-technical workforce adopt secure, technology practices through data-driven insights, training, and specialized programming that inspire meaningful behavior change. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week. jobs.title: Assistant Editor, Data Journalism
jobs.description_text: The Data Journalism team is looking for an experienced journalist with editing, management and data analysis skills to serve as an assistant editor. You'll help to run a group of data journalists who collaborate across the newsroom. You'll also advise on analyses conducted elsewhere in the newsroom. You should be obsessed with detail and rigor, display a knack for lifting stories to the next level and care deeply about developing your colleagues' talents. Collaboration is at the heart of this role; the Data Journalism team works with virtually every other desk in the newsroom. We'll expect you to deftly navigate these partnerships, which require crisp communication, a problem-solving attitude and a dash of diplomacy. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week. We have a preference for candidates who will work in New York City, with a secondary preference for Washington, DC. Important application requirement: Please submit a cover letter that describes your qualifications in the context of three stories (or projects) you helped to shape. For each, please provide a link to the work and describe your contributions in one to three paragraphs. Your cover letter should not exceed four pages in total. Within that limit, you are also welcome to provide a more traditional (but brief) description of your career and talents. jobs.title: Audience Editor, Climate and Science
jobs.description_text: We are looking for an audience editor to join the newsroom Audience team and partner with our Climate and Science desks to help them continue to reach more readers and deepen our engagement with those readers. This editor will work with the desk to inform coverage, both day-to-day and long-term, suggesting timely stories as well as evergreen topics, with an eye toward framing. They will help maximize distribution through search strategies and social programming, and by pitching internally to the homepage, newsletters and other alerts. And they will track data for the desk, using analytical skills to provide context and recommendations to the editors. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. Responsibilities: Audience strategy & growth: Partner with senior editors to inform coverage decisions, suggesting timely stories, evergreen topics, and longer-term franchises that resonate with reader interest and important news moments, with a keen eye toward framing and formats. Identify coverage and format opportunities that will attract new readers, particularly those who may not currently view The New York Times as a regular news source. You will bridge the gap between analytical tasks and the strategic implementation of corporate compensation programs. You will manage specific client group relationships, lead smaller compensation projects, and provide recommendations that directly inform pay decisions and policy administration. jobs.title: Deputy Editor, Well
jobs.description_text: The Well desk is seeking a Deputy Editor to join its core leadership team to oversee editorial operations, including day-to-day scheduling, long-term planning and managing editors and reporters. As our Deputy Editor, you will help the desk to pursue ambitious targets, set priorities, and home in on a consistent voice and mission. You'll push Well editors and reporters to collaborate internally and with the newsroom, and help guide inter-desk collaboration. You will do first edits on stories and top-read our report. You will also serve as the desk deputy and can run all aspects of the desk as a proxy for the Editor of Well, when necessary. You will report to the Well desk's Editor. jobs.title: Designer, Marketing (Games)
jobs.description_text: We are seeking a Marketing Designer to help bring to life the full-funnel creative strategy and execution for our Games subscription offering. This is a hands-on design role for a creative who can translate the value of all we offer — independent journalism and world-class lifestyle products — into clear, compelling campaigns that drive performance and deepen engagement with Games. Reporting to the Associate Creative Director, Games, Marketing, you will work closely with writers, designers and our audio and video teams, as well as partners in marketing and media strategy, product design, audience insights and brand identity. You'll contribute to integrated campaigns across the full subscriber journey — from full-funnel product launches to subscriber acquisition campaigns to app store optimization efforts and more. We are looking for a designer who is passionate about both exceptional craft and the collaborative process it takes to create it. You thrive at the intersection of brand and performance, are excited to contribute directly to growth and product marketing initiatives, and partner with more senior creative leaders on the team. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office three days per week. Responsibilities: Contribute to the development and execution of conceptual, visually compelling campaigns and always-on marketing creative for Games, ensuring work supports awareness, consideration, conversion and retention

jobs.title: Director, Commerce Partnerships (Temp)
jobs.description_text: Wirecutter strives to be the most trusted product recommendation service on the internet. We obsessively test and report on thousands of items each year to recommend the best of everything. Our goal is to save you time and eliminate the stress of shopping, whether you’re looking for everyday gear or gifts for loved ones. We work with total editorial independence. That means nothing appears on the site as a recommendation unless our writers and editors have deemed it the best through our rigorous reporting and testing. Wirecutter was founded in September 2011 and acquired by The New York Times Company in October 2016. Wirecutter is mission-driven and reader-supported; learn more about us here. About the Role Wirecutter is looking for a strategic and operationally oriented partnerships leader who is passionate about driving performance-based results that provide the best buying experience on Wirecutter Picks. The Director, Commerce Partnerships reports directly to the Executive Director, Commerce and is the team leader responsible for business development, partnerships and affiliate operations. You will emphasize building career development plans through active mentorship of the team, and working across the organization to achieve our goals and priorities. This role is open to remote hiring. This is a temporary role running from September 2026 - May 2027. Responsibilities: Oversee the strategic development of Wirecutter’s affiliate revenue growth strategies to meet EPC targets

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office 3+ days per week. jobs.title: Editor, Cannonball
jobs.description_text: The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp. The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work. This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. jobs.title: Editor, The Interview
jobs.description_text: Over the past two years, “The Interview” has made itself a trustworthy New York Times brand and a destination, where artists (Mick Jagger, Nicolas Cage, Charlize Theron), politicians (Zohran Mamdani, Chuck Schumer), athletes (Karl-Anthony Towns), influential figures in the media (Megyn Kelly, Andrew Schulz, Tucker Carlson), at the center of a story (Scott Pelley, Gisele Pelicot) and beyond sit down for thoughtful, wide-ranging, challenging, fun, news-making video conversations about their lives and ideas. We are seeking an experienced editor to, in collaboration with the executive producer, guide the editorial selection, writing and structure of the show. You will need to be a total omnivore — as excited about and adept at figuring out the best approach for an interview with John Fetterman as Lena Dunham — and a positive, motivating leader on the team. You need to believe in the power of good conversation to reveal subjects and illuminate ideas and also understand how to structure those conversations to be as compelling as possible — which will at times be free-wheeling and loose and at other times tighter and more targeted. You must have a keen understanding of the moment — in the news, in the culture — and know how to translate that understanding for a show that works on a few different tracks at once, with some bookings coming together far in advance and others really responding to a news moment. jobs.title: Editor, Weekend Audience
jobs.description_text: The New York Times is looking for an editor to help lead our teams across our flagship social accounts and search, with a focus on weekend programming. A successful candidate for this role will bring expertise in all things audience growth off-platform, including search and social platforms as well as emerging ones, a strong sense of news judgment and audience signals, as well as a keen eye for off-platform photos, graphics and videos. The editor will help establish a vision for shaping and targeting our journalism for different platforms to ensure that the full breadth of Times journalism finds audiences on weekends. This role bridges tactical execution and high-level strategy. Leading the work of a small team of off-platform editors during the weekends, you will work story by story — including helping to program our social accounts — and think more broadly about the mix of our off-platform social report, and how it should or should not differ from the weekday to the weekends. You will also have a hands-on role in ensuring our journalism appears across high-demand topics for users who seek news, but haven't yet made The Times their destination for news. This person will work Wednesday through Sunday. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. The executive assistant will manage complex scheduling and logistics, organize priorities and follow-through, coordinate across senior leaders and departments, draft correspondence, support projects with research and project management, and serve as a trusted representative of the masthead leader's office. The ideal candidate exercises sophisticated judgment, anticipates needs, communicates with discretion and professionalism, and is comfortable working in a fast-paced, highly collaborative newsroom environment. jobs.title: Fact Checker, Shows
jobs.description_text: The New York Times Shows department is hiring a staff editor to fact check episodes of Hard Fork, both in video and audio formats. You will work with producers and editors to check facts and assertions, with extra attention to the tone and context in which they're delivered. You are comfortable working in print, audio and video mediums in a fast-paced news environment. We're looking for exceptional news judgment, an investigator's mind and the ability to dive into unfamiliar material on deadline. And while we value deliberate, careful checking, speed is also important. The fact checker will be part of a small group of producers and editors, so collegiality, diplomacy and a collaborative spirit are a must. This is a part-time role for 20 hours a week to start. It could scale up over time. You will report to the Executive Producer of Hard Fork. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office each week. jobs.title: FOIA Editor
jobs.description_text: The New York Times is looking for a FOIA editor to oversee and guide our strategy of using the Freedom of Information Act and other local, state and federal public records laws to obtain information from governmental and public entities. You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience. You will help track and expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals, and will work closely with the Legal department to identify efforts that merit litigation support. This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office each week. The person will also work closely with our bureau in Washington and make periodic visits there. You will be responsible for fact checking and researching puzzles and related copy for digital and print publication for New York Times Games. In addition to ensuring assigned work is accurate, they are experienced enough in solving our puzzles that they can catch issues with the solution or other gameplay. Responsibilities may include reviewing notes from other fact checkers or testers, and working on existing New York Times puzzles or a new beta game. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City office. Why should you apply? This is an opportunity to help shape products that people love. New York Times Games is a unique brand, with a portfolio of hit games with millions of fans. The fact checker will work on games cross-functionally with puzzle editors, writers, product designers, engineers, marketers and social media experts. Responsibilities: Check factual assertions in assigned puzzle copy - including clues, questions, directions, categories, titles and themes. jobs.description_text: The Graphics department at The New York Times is looking for a versatile, experienced visual journalist to report, design and create graphics and multimedia stories, with a primary focus on breaking news and fast-turn news response. You will execute visual coverage on major breaking stories, producing maps, charts, diagrams and interactive graphics on deadline. Your work may also include statistical visualizations, video, photography and animation. You will identify visual story angles, analyze data, and collaborate closely with Graphics colleagues and newsroom journalists across desks. This role combines quick-turn breaking news execution with high-impact journalism. You may also be required to work weekends. The Graphics department is a diverse group of journalists and visual thinkers with creative backgrounds ranging from architecture to cartography to computer science. We are curious about all kinds of things and seek to find individuals who bring their own curiosity to bear in creative approaches to storytelling. This is an in-office position based in New York City, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. Applications should include links to a portfolio or work samples to demonstrate the creation of visual journalism. Please feel free to describe your role in specific projects in your cover letter. jobs.description_text: The New York Times Graphics team is looking for a reporter with extensive open-source and investigative reporting skills to turn raw evidence into impactful visual stories. You have a track record for uncovering exclusive information off the news. The Graphics team is a leader in using spatial and visual techniques on investigative stories, and we're looking for someone who is passionate about accountability journalism using cutting-edge reporting techniques. Below are a few examples of the kinds of stories that you will be a part of: An exclusive look at the failed columns of the Midtown Manhattan near-collapse A 3-D analysis of why firefighters' lines of sight were limited in the deadly LaGuardia Crash An investigation into the mass graves in Syria An investigation into the causes of a Miami building collapse A spatial investigation into a deadly fire in the Bronx A forensic analysis of an apartment building collapse in the Turkey earthquake Working with journalists on the Graphics team and across the newsroom, you will play an important role in shaping visual reconstructions and investigations that rely on spatial analysis or use 3-D modeling. You will gather and analyze evidence for stories across a wide range of topics for both quick-turn stories as well as longer-term enterprise. jobs.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Shows
jobs.description_text: About the Role The New York Times' Motion Graphics team focuses on elevating how animated graphics and motion design are used in our video journalism. Working in close collaboration with Video, Shows and Graphics, the team responds to the demands of stories and formats across the newsroom—from news explainers and visual investigations to enterprise series and shows. As a member of Digital News Design's Motion Graphics team, you will focus on work for Shows, a department created to expand the reach of The Times's audio and video shows. You will collaborate with reporters, editors, producers, art directors and show hosts to craft motion assets and visuals for our expanding roster of shows across a range of formats and platforms. You will be responsible for identifying creative needs and producing a range of design assets, including motion graphics, typography, animations, and mogert templates. In consultation with editors and other newsroom leaders, you'll exercise journalistic judgment and visual creativity to innovate and ensure accuracy, clarity, and validity of the content presented. Design team members are expected not only to make exceptional contributions to our journalism, but also to engage with others to foster an environment of learning and constructive dialogue about our work. This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance

jobs.title: Hollywood News and Awards Reporter, Culture
jobs.description_text: The Culture Desk is seeking a nimble journalist to report on the movie awards season, and report out news stories and investigations about the consumer-facing side of Hollywood throughout the year. The position encompasses writing the Projectionist awards season column and reporting live from the red carpet during the Oscars and other awards shows, as well as appearing in videos. But awards season is only part of the job. You will be expected to cover the news and controversies of pop culture throughout the year, deliver investigations and enterprise stories, and write features about the latest releases and how they impact audiences and society. Your work should drive conversations about Hollywood and entertainment both before and after a premiere. We are looking for someone who is well-sourced in Hollywood, has deep expertise about movie awards and understands both how Hollywood works and how its output can generate larger conversations and controversies. Ideally, the reporter has the ability to cover fast-breaking news of interest to culturally curious readers. Night and weekend work will be a necessary part of this coverage. The reporter will work in coordination with the Times business reporters who cover Hollywood.
